analysis: His default skill set is neutralized by large greens but there’s been enough mojo in the last two months to supersede plug-and-play analysis. And even though he scuffled with 72s on the weekend at TPC Southwind, he managed a T19.

After quietly collecting FedExCup points for most of the season, the Swede has bum-rushed his way into consideration for a spot in the TOUR Championship. With a T18, a T7 and a T3 in his last three starts, he’s 34th in the ranks.

With a commitment to the BMW Championship on deck, he could get away with a third-to-last-place finish at TPC Southwind. Now he’ll want to lock in ahead of giving his fourth FedExCup title a whirl at the TOUR Championship.

The Brit not only remains in tiptop form what with seven consecutive top-15 finishes (top 10s in the last two), it’s where he wants to be in his unique quest to become the first FedExCup champion to successfully defend the title.

He was promised to cash at TPC Southwind, but didn’t squander it with a steady T12. It would have been surprising if he did. In position to capitalize on a career year, his focus is elevated across the final fortnight.

Playoffs season is his season, and the 2021 FedExCup champ just launched into this one with a T12 at TPC Southwind. That piggybacked a T8 at the Rocket Classic, so while he needs a strong finish to advance, he has momentum.

His Sunday 74 at TPC Southwind was the highest final round among those who finished inside the top 25, and he still nabbed a T5. It’s his third top five of 2026 and fourth top 15 in his last five starts. Built for Bellerive.

His win at the Genesis Scottish Open was a reflection of his affinity for links-style golf and a recommitment to his craft, but his body of work all summer speaks to his talent. The reset has renewed confidence for this scorer.

Got back in gear with a T5 at the FedEx St. Jude Championship where he led the field in putts per greens in regulation. With sizeable targets in St. Louis, his presence looms large to pile up and convert on scoring opportunities.

Sufficiently back in form with consecutive top 10s upon arrival, even if a month apart. The bonus upshot is that he’s rested to make a run. Still sniped by an untimely round too often, his firepower is undeniable across 72 holes.

Seemingly has the opposition right where he wants it in advance of the TOUR Championship. Chased his runner-up at the Rocket Classic with a T7 at the FedEx St. Jude on Sunday, both with a sublime tee-to-green attack.

Although he hasn’t picked off a victory this season, the runner-up at TPC Southwind has been a machine en route to a trio of seconds and two thirds among 11 top 10s. Leading the TOUR with 60 red numbers and 49 sub-70s.

Continues to pour it on without showing signs of stopping. Since a T14 at The Open, he hasn’t rested as he’s added respective results of T3, T5, T7 and T7. Complementing efficient ball-striking with above-average putting.

Winless since capturing the last Match Play in 2023 but he was beaten by only five guys in three of his last four starts, two of which in majors. Bellerive’s large greens feed into his strengths on approach and with the putter.

Every team that makes the MLB postseason lines up its ace for game 1, so it’s not shocking in the slightest that the FedExCup leader and world’s top-ranked talent tossed a gem in the opener. Again the player to beat, unanimously.
